subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should the public web-tool egress boundary be: a narrow `web_fetch` hostname allowlist, managed-proxy ownership, or a cross-tool fetch/search/browser policy with allow and deny semantics?
rationale: This creates an operator-trusted security/config surface, and the active related PRs encode different security boundaries that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped `web_fetch` Allowlist First
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while leaving deny domains, managed search, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make Managed Proxy The Boundary
options.body: Pause local `web_fetch` config work and route app-owned egress policy through managed proxy behavior instead.

options.title: Design Cross-Tool Policy First
options.body: Require a broader design covering fetch, search, browser, provider fallback, redirects, caches, plugin HTTP, and deny semantics before implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped `web_fetch` Allowlist First
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while leaving deny domains, managed search, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history across SSRF, guarded fetch, and the open hostname-allowlist implementation path.
